Endpoint registry and API-Registry Explorer

The endpoint registry maps the logical names SATOM uses to the REST paths each product and API version serves; the API-Registry Explorer lets you browse and edit that catalog and send requests to an appliance.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsregistry.view registry.edit registry.execute_write
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → API-Registry Explorer (URL /web/api-explorer/); API versions at /web/registry/versions; reconcile at /web/registry/reconcile
On this page
  • Overview
  • Where the catalog comes from
  • Permissions
  • Using the API-Registry Explorer
  • Send a request
  • Edit the catalog
  • Reconcile
  • API versions

Overview#

SATOM never hard-codes an appliance REST path. Code asks for a logical name (for example a server-policy collection) and the endpoint registry returns the path (URN) for that product and API version. When Fortinet moves an endpoint, one catalog row changes — not the code.

Concept Meaning
Logical name The key code uses; letters, digits, _, - and . only
URN The absolute API path the appliance serves, starting with /
API version The protocol generation (v2.0 for FortiWeb, v1 for FortiADC by default)
Product fortiweb, fortiadc, fortianalyzer, fortiauthenticator
Baseline The shipped catalog for a product, pinned to one firmware build, in app/registry/baselines/<product>.json

The registry key is (product, API version, name).

Where the catalog comes from#

  1. 1Shipped baselineapp/registry/baselines/<product>.json, sealed with a SHA-256
  2. 2Start-upmissing baseline is inserted; registry reconciled to the active baseline
  3. 3Operator editsrows an operator created, edited or disabled are never touched again by a baseline
  4. 4Readsfrom the registry_endpoints table, cached per worker for 60 s
  5. 5Fallbackif the database is unreachable or empty, the shipped baseline is served directly
  • A row written by a baseline is marked baseline:<product>@<version> (older rows seed); a row an operator touched carries the operator's name.
  • Removing an endpoint is a soft delete (disabled, not deleted), so no seed can bring back a name an operator removed.
  • An edit made on one gunicorn worker is visible on the others within 60 seconds.
  • Only the FortiWeb and FortiADC catalogs can be edited. FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator catalogs are seeded but read-only.

Baselines are maintained with flask apilib baseline … (status, promote, apply, check, resolve, export, adopt); see API library.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the Explorer, browse the catalog, send GET requests registry.view (the page opens in the FortiWeb ADOM)
Send POST / PUT / DELETE / PATCH registry.execute_write
New / edit / disable / restore a catalog endpoint; Reconcile; API versions page (view, export, rebuild, declare, review, forget) registry.edit (checked as the coarse registry_edit key)
Harvest this appliance now, discovery load appliances.apply
CLI-coverage block, live view and capture (they return device configuration) backups.create or backups.restore (coarse backup key)

Without registry.edit the API Menu shows no edit buttons and the editing routes return 403. Without registry.execute_write the write methods are disabled in the method list and the server answers "The "Execute write API calls" permission is required for non-GET methods."

Without registry.view the Explorer page and GET requests are refused, and the sidebar does not show the link. Seeded profiles: readonly and operator hold registry.view; only admin holds registry.edit and registry.execute_write.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the API-Registry Explorer and its GET requests now require View registry (registry.view) instead of sign-in alone (the sidebar hides the link without it), and the disable/restore toggle on the FortiWeb page acts on FortiWeb rows only.

Using the API-Registry Explorer#

The page (title API-Registry Explorer) has four areas:

Area Purpose
API Menu Catalog tree by section. Filter with Filter endpoints…; Only what this build serves hides endpoints the selected appliance's firmware does not serve. Editors see New Endpoint, edit and disable buttons, and a Disabled list with restore buttons.
Request Appliance, method, path, Key Filter (mkey), Request Body (JSON), Execute Request
Response / History The JSON answer, Copy; recent requests in this browser, Clear
Build / Fields on this build What the API library knows about the selected appliance's firmware build, and the fields of the selected endpoint

Send a request#

  1. Pick the Appliance.
  2. Choose an endpoint in the API Menu (or type a path).
  3. Pick the method; for writes, enter the Request Body (JSON).
  4. Click Execute Request.

Every executed request is written to the audit log. Before sending, SATOM checks the API library for the appliance's exact build:

Library verdict Result
Served Sent
Unknown (build or endpoint never measured) Sent with a warning: "Unverified: … — the appliance decides."
Absent (measured or vendor data says not served) Refused with HTTP 409 "Refused: … does not serve … Send again with confirm_unserved to override." The page asks for confirmation and re-sends.

Appliances whose address is loopback or link-local are refused ("Appliance host is not permitted.").

⚠️Warning — Writes go straight to the appliance

The Explorer is a raw REST client. A POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH is sent as typed, with no preview and no rollback. Use the feature pages (which preview and audit changes) for routine work.

Edit the catalog#

  1. Click New Endpoint (or the edit button on a leaf).
  2. Enter the Logical name, the URN / API path (absolute, starting with /) and the API version.
  3. Click Save. The flash says Endpoint "" saved.

Disable an endpoint with Disable catalog endpoint (soft delete); restore it from the Disabled list. On the FortiWeb page this toggle only acts on FortiWeb rows. Validation messages:

Message Cause
Name and URN are both required. A field is empty
Endpoint name may only contain letters, digits, "_", "-" and ".". Invalid name
URN must be an absolute API path (e.g. /api/v2.0/cmdb/... or /api/load_balance_pool). Path does not start with /
An endpoint named "<name>" already exists (<urn>). Duplicate in the same product and API version

Reconcile#

Reconcile (/web/registry/reconcile) reads what the rediscovery sweep measured on every live appliance and proposes changes; it changes nothing until you apply.

Bucket Meaning
Proposals Not found on every live appliance — candidate for disabling
Divergent Absent on one appliance, served by another (firmware/feature difference — do not disable)
Partial Absent where measured, but not measured everywhere
Unproven Enabled, in the sweep plan, never measured
Unsweepable Enabled but not in the sweep plan, so no sweep can answer
Verified Served by at least one appliance

"Absent" (the appliance says the path does not exist) is never confused with "error" (transport, authentication, licence), and a ledger made mostly of errors is not used as evidence.

API versions#

API versions (/web/registry/versions) compares the API surface per full firmware version (for example 7.6.8 against 8.0.5), because one API version (v2.0) can still differ in fields between builds. You can export the comparison as CSV or PDF, declare a firmware version by hand, review recorded disappearances, and rebuild the export file used by the offline CLI (data/api_matrix/<product>.json).

The FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator workspaces have their own API pages built on the same catalog; see Product API pages.

Advanced Old URLs

The standalone Registry page was merged into the Explorer: /registry and /registry/<section> redirect to the Explorer. Paths without the /web prefix (for example /api-explorer) are rewritten to the FortiWeb-prefixed path.

Advanced Reads from code

Services resolve names per build through registry.loader (resolve_for, registry_for). flask apilib baseline resolve --product P [--build X] NAME shows which URN a name resolves to on a build and on what authority; flask apilib baseline check reports drift between registry, baseline and fleet evidence and exits 1 on drift.

#registry#endpoint registry#api explorer#urn#logical name#catalog#baseline#reconcile#api versions#execute write#rest client
